rows: What are you planning for the landing? That is the bit you have not sold me.
Brawling is a habit that needs a plan. What is yours after the first big move?
A risk is a choice about what happens next. Tell me what happens next.
Slow is a decision I respect. Make it on purpose, and I will respect it more.
The people deserve a match that is looked after, and I want to look after it with you.
Short version: I have seen what happens when the plan is missing. Make sure yours is not.
I have been around long enough to know what a good plan looks like. This is not yet a good plan.
Look at the stance. Balanced. Good. Now tell me where the weight goes after it.
You say technique. Tell me what you do when the first attempt does not land.
Strikes are part of the job. Know what they set up, and know what you do after.
A risk without an exit plan is only a hope. What is your exit?
A stall gives you time to think. Use it to think about the next moment, not to hide.
The people want a contest with a clear ending. Make sure you can deliver one.
You say I am a worrier. I am a person who checks the landing. Those are different things.
You are proud of your {strength}. Good. Be proud of it, and be careful with it.
I have watched your {strength}, and I would like to see what you do when it goes wrong.
You kept calm. Good. That is the single most useful thing you can do on a night like this.
Fair. That is a good plan, as far as it goes. Keep going.
I could argue about that. I would rather ask what happens after it.
One fall. Keep me down. Then tell me how you will get off me.
On the mat, the plan matters more than the move. Tell me the plan.
Grounded or standing, what happens next is your responsibility.
Stay in front of me, and show me the next step before you take it.
Good answer. That is the sort of thing I want to hear.
You have not answered. What happens next? Tell me that much.
Fair. That is a sensible point, and I will hold you to it.
I accept that. We will check the landing at the bell.
I will wrestle this match with a clear plan, and I will not leave the landing to chance.
My approach is careful. You will see the plan on the night.
Whatever happens, I want to be sure you are all right afterwards.
It is not finished. The plan is still open.
I have one more question, and you will answer it when the bell rings.
